levels.name: First words
levels.sentenceLengthHint: strictly max 7 words per sentence, simple subject-verb-object
grammarAllowed: present of ser and estar (soc, ets, és, estic, està)

definite and indefinite articles (el, la, els, les, un, una). el and la elide to l' before a vowel or h (l'home, l'aigua, l'hora) - never 'el home'. The one exception: la does NOT elide before an unstressed i- or u- (la idea, la universitat, la humitat), though it does before a stressed one (l'illa)

plurals: -s by default; feminines in -a take -es (casa/cases); a word ending in a STRESSED -s, -ç, -x or -ig takes -os and doubles a single s after the stressed vowel (gos/gossos, peix/peixos, feliç/feliços, mes/mesos). A word ending in an UNSTRESSED -s is invariable (el llapis/els llapis, el dilluns/els dilluns, el temps/els temps) - never 'dillunsos'. Adjectives agree in gender and number
present indicative of first-conjugation -ar verbs (parlo, parles, parla)
simple questions with què, qui, on, com, quan
negation with no

levels.name: Daily life
grammarAllowed: present indicative of all three conjugations, including the incoative -eix- type (serveixo, prefereixes)
the irregular presents a beginner needs: tenir (tinc), fer (faig), anar (vaig), poder (puc), voler (vull), venir (vinc), dir (dic), saber (sé), veure (veig)
possessives (el meu, la teva, els seus)
hi ha for existence, and the contractions al, del, pel
the periphrastic past (vaig menjar, vas anar) - this, not the simple past, is how Catalan speaks about the past
cardinal numbers, days, months, telling the time
prepositions a, de, en, amb, per, sense, fins

Catalan has no Spanish-style personal a with a plain direct object: write 'veig la Maria', never 'veig a la Maria'. But do keep the a where the verb governs it (trucar a algú, telefonar a algú) and before a strong personal pronoun ('et veig a tu')

levels.name: Short stories
levels.sentenceLengthHint: max 12 words per sentence; at most one subordinate clause
grammarAllowed: imperfect indicative (parlava, tenia, era, feia) for description and habit, contrasted with the periphrastic past for completed events
the perfect with haver (he menjat, hem arribat) for events within today
singular weak pronouns em, et, es, el, la, li, and reflexive verbs (llevar-se, dir-se, rentar-se)
the pronouns hi and en, including en for partitives (en vull dos)
future indicative (parlaré, tindré, faré)
comparatives and superlatives (més ... que, menys ... que, tan ... com, el més)
connectors però, perquè, quan, mentre, també, tampoc
verbs with a velar stem must use it: tinc/tingui, vinc/vingui, venc/vengui, ric/rigui

levels.name: Everyday texts
levels.sentenceLengthHint: max 14 words per sentence; subordinate clauses allowed
grammarAllowed: conditional (parlaria, voldria, m'agradaria) for politeness and hypothesis
present subjunctive after voler que, esperar que, caldre que, and after quan with future reference
plural weak pronouns ens, us, els, les, and combined pronouns (me'l, l'hi, se'n) with correct apostrophes and hyphens
relative clauses with que, qui, on
the gerund for simultaneity (tot caminant) - never for consecutive actions
impersonal es (es parla català, es ven pa)
verbal periphrases haver de, poder, voler, tornar a, acabar de
ela geminada is written with the interpunct: col·legi, intel·ligent - never 'colegi' or 'col.legi'
